title: The time courses of runners' recovery-stress responses after a mountain ultra-marathon: Do appraisals matter?
authors: Gaudino M, Martinent G, Millet GY, Nicolas M
population: 29 mountain ultra-marathon runners, one measurement within two days before the race and six measurements within the month after
findings: Seven-wave one-month longitudinal design with multilevel growth curve analysis.

Significant linear increases of general and total recovery and significant linear decreases of general, sport-specific and total stress over the month; a U-shaped (positive quadratic) effect of time on specific recovery.

Primary appraisal positively predicted sport-specific recovery and total, general and sport-specific stress, and negatively predicted total and general recovery; secondary appraisal negatively predicted total and general stress.
The abstract states trajectories and predictors but gives no day-by-day scores.
limitations: Exact questionnaire items not in the abstract; no numeric day-by-day values; subjective scale only; the abstract does not say how many runners were lost to follow-up.
implications: A subjective recovery-stress scale improves roughly linearly over a month after a mountain ultra, supporting a multi-week monitoring horizon after 100 km and 100 miles, with ratings used as a trend and not a single-day threshold.

Pre-race appraisals predicted recovery-stress scores, so the same rating may mean different things for different people; compare a runner's rating with that runner's own recent ratings, not an absolute cutoff (inference from the appraisal result).

verification.notes: Crossref gives authors Gaudino M, Martinent G, Millet GY, Nicolas M; the record's author list (Gaudino P, Sales, Brisswalter, Hausswirth) was wrong and is corrected. Abstract re-read (PMID 30638146); trajectories and predictors match. Study race distance is not given in the abstract.
